about: Reviewed misspellings in the era sheets (data/hist-eras.js, aourednik/historical-basemaps). Each entry corrects a string to a spelling the same corpus uses on uncorrected features; the corrected feature keeps upstream's word as `u`. Applied by node scripts/build-hist-eras.mjs (every build) and --spelling (the committed file); held by npm run check:histeras (scripts/histeras/spelling.mjs). Found 2026-10-07 by listing the names drawn on the same or adjacent ground in neighbouring sheets that differ by a slip of one or two letters; the pairs that are real distinctions (Malay/Malays, Sinhalese kingdom/kingdoms, Austronesian/Austronesians, Ainu/Ainus, Papuan/Papuans, Maori/Maoris, Tokugawa Shogunate/shogunate, Chinese Warlords/warlords) are not corrected.

corrections.why: Transposed letters (and a doubled t) for Scotland, drawn on the same ground as «Scotland» on the 1279, 1300 and 1400 sheets; the Kingdom of Scotland is the polity of 1650-1707 (union with England, 1 May 1707).
A doubled t for Scotland, drawn on the same ground as «Scotland» on the 1279, 1300 and 1400 sheets (the Kingdom of Scotland under the Stewarts).
Transposed vowels for the Beothuk of Newfoundland, whom the same cartographer writes «Beothuk» on the 800, 900 and 1279-1600 sheets on the same ground.
A dropped o in «Proto-Altaic», the spelling the same cartographer uses on the bc500 sheet for the same pastoralists on the same steppe ground.
